referents.why: 'me' in Moses' own speech (the imperative 'honor yourself over me'): the speaker is Moses
second masculine singular 'you' in Moses' speech; the one spoken to is Pharaoh
possessive 'your' with officials: the addressee of the speech, Pharaoh
the implied 'you' of the imperative is the person spoken to, Pharaoh (second masculine singular)
first common singular 'I will pray' in Moses' question: Moses
feminine plural 'they will remain' agrees with the frogs, the things removed from Pharaoh and left in the river

links.why: the infinitive gives what the praying asks for; the purpose form excludes a clause of saying or asking where the infinitive is what is said, and prayer to God is such a case
links.category: prayer content read as the request

links.why: what Moses prays for is what is said: the infinitive is the content of the request (R1)
links.category: prayer content read as the request

links.why: Moses said: the imperative clause is said content (R1)

cl5 is not a clause of this verse (it has cl0 to cl4); the builder link runs from the previous verse. Then is within a verse only; the change of speaker from Pharaoh to Moses is the episode rung, not a then link

groups.why: one turn of Moses to Pharaoh; sender and addressee are right

none_fit.what: an exception marked by רַק ('only'): the frogs are removed except those that remain in the Nile. No link type covers it: but_rather takes כִּי אִם and unless takes לוּלֵא

none_fit.where: cl4, 'only in the River they will remain', inside Moses's question
none_fit.what: a restriction on what the removal covers (the frogs removed except those that stay in the Nile). No link type carries an exception to a purpose clause: 'unless' is a condition, and 'but_rather' needs a negative clause with כִּי אִם.
'only in the Nile they will remain' is an exception to the removal ('except for those in the Nile'). elaborates gives its detail, but no link type states an exception to a request.

cant_tell.what: whether the infinitive cl3 is the content of the prayer (as recorded) or its purpose
cant_tell.why: prayer is speech to God and the purpose form excludes what is said; a reader may still take it as the purpose of praying
